newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnian authorities suspend unpopular curfew.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian authorities suspend unpopular curfew.

text.p: Bosnia has suspended an unpopular curfew in Sarajevo and other towns that has remained despite the end of the 1992-95 conflict, media reports said on Monday.

The Interior Ministry said the suspension would last until February 15 because of celebrations and cultural events marking Christmas, New Year's Day, and the Islamic Ramadan religious holidays in January.
The nightly 11 p.m. curfew is disliked and independent radio stations have criticised the authorities for keeping it in peacetime.
Alexander Ivanko, a spokesman for United Nations police monitors, said he hoped the curfew would end permanently.
The ministry said it would decide when suspension expires.
The move follows the federation parliament's abolition last week of the "state of imminent war danger" on its territory.
